entities.evidence: Kenan’s son, introduced in Genesis 5:12, is sixty-five when he fathers Jared here. The source tag agrees.
The verse names Jared as Mahalalel’s son in the genealogy before the Flood. His parentage distinguishes him from Jered son of Mered in 1 Chronicles 4:18. The source tag agrees.

analysis.evidence: מַהֲלַלְאֵל is the subject of וַיְחִי. The following חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה gives the sixty-five years he lived before he fathered Jared.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: live for a stated span of time

analysis.evidence: מַהֲלַלְאֵל is the subject of וַיְחִי and וַיּוֹלֶד. The verse continues Kenan’s genealogy by naming Mahalalel as the father of Jared at age sixty-five.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים means “five years.” The following וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה adds sixty years, giving Mahalalel’s age as sixty-five when he fathered Jared.
חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים means “five years.” With וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה (“and sixty years”), it gives Mahalalel’s age when he fathered Jared.
In חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה, “five years and sixty years,” וְ joins the two parts of Mahalalel’s age. The marked word contributes sixty to the total of sixty-five years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a cardinal numeral, plural in form, common gender, absolute state.

analysis.evidence: The marked שָׁנָה follows וְשִׁשִּׁים ‘and sixty’. Together with חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים ‘five years’, it gives Mahalalel’s age of sixty-five when he fathered Jared.
מַהֲלַלְאֵל is the subject, and אֶת marks יָרֶד as the direct object. After giving Mahalalel’s age as sixty-five, the verse says that he fathered Jared.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת יָרֶד, “he fathered Jared,” אֶת marks the personal name יָרֶד as the definite direct object of וַיּוֹלֶד.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for יֶרֶד linked to the consonantal root ירד.
draft.definition: Jared is the personal name of Mahalalel’s son in Genesis 5:15.
draft.evidence: וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת יָרֶד means “he fathered Jared.” The genealogy identifies the bearer and gives no explanation of the name’s origin.

analysis.evidence: Mahalalel is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, “he fathered.” The direct-object marker אֶת introduces יָרֶד as the name of his son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in the verse-final pausal form יָרֶד, without prefix or suffix.
